answer: A observatory log with telescope booking history works as the gate: nights booked at one observatory across years. Each of 549 aliases needs its own booking histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The relic check runs in the open: 549 fakes pay the full price 549 times, one honest agent pays once, and the ledge trail in the ledger makes the zephyr cost visible to everyone.
